I am 72 years old, been on this land 50 years. My son works in the city so it's just me and my wife on 6 mu. I cannot work as hard as before, so I keep things simple and do what I know works.

Of my 6 mu, I plant 4 mu to wheat-maize double crop — that is my main grain. The other 2 mu I keep in cotton, same as my neighbors on the east side of the village. Cotton price has not been great, but I have the seed and know the work, and my wife helps with picking.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant Jimai 22 type — improved seed, I buy from the dealer in town every two years. Last autumn I put about 40 jin (20 kg) of compound 15-15-15 per mu before ploughing, plus some urea in spring at jointing, maybe 25 jin (12-13 kg) per mu. So nitrogen comes to around 18 kg, phosphorus 8 kg, potassium 6 kg per mu. I water twice — once before winter, once at jointing. If spring is dry I add a third. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, this year I hope for the same.

**Maize (summer):** After wheat I plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, no-till direct seeding right into the stubble. I side-dress urea at the big bell stage, about 50 jin (25 kg) per mu, that is the main feeding. Phosphorus and potassium I already put plenty in the wheat so maize gets the leftover, I add a little compound at planting, maybe 20 jin. One irrigation at tasseling if no rain. Spray once for borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

**Cotton (spring):** I use hybrid Bt cotton seed, already have it. Plough the 2 mu once, put compound fertilizer in the row, about 50 jin per mu before planting, then topdress urea at flowering. Cotton needs potassium for bolls so I add potash too. Irrigate 3 times — seedling, flowering, boll-filling. Pesticide — even with Bt I still spray 4-5 times for aphids and mirids. Yield maybe 220 kg seed cotton per mu, depends on weather at bolling.

I don't change much from last year. Fertilizer prices are high but I'd rather spend the money than risk a thin harvest — at my age I cannot recover a lost season.
